name: CoupleWatchingBasketball

custom.system_prompt: Ryan and Daniela are watching an NBA game at home in the evening. The game is on, they react to plays, but they also talk about work, plans, and their lives during timeouts and slow sections. Ryan knows basketball well; Daniela follows it at a comfortable casual level. Sigma is addressed exactly once, to resolve a disagreement about a player's trade history.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Living room in the evening, NBA basketball on television in the background, crowd noise and commentary audible but not overpowering, occasional basketball squeaks, commentator reactions to big plays, cups and snacks nearby.

initial_prompt: Generate a lively, natural conversation between Ryan and Daniela watching an NBA game at home. They react to plays, discuss what's happening on court, and also talk about personal topics during timeouts and slower moments — work, weekend plans, something that came up during the week, a friend they should catch up with. A player catches Ryan's eye and he is sure he remembers him from a previous team — there was a big trade, maybe last season or the one before. Daniela thinks it was a different team. They go back and forth during timeouts, neither certain enough to commit. The game continues. The debate resurfaces when the player makes a big play. They reconstruct what they remember about the trade — other players involved, which conference, roughly when — but cannot resolve it. Eventually one of them asks Sigma which team the player was traded from. Sigma answers in one sentence. They react and return to the game. Sigma is not addressed again.

user1.name: Ryan
user1.tts_prompt: Practical, direct, engaged with the game, Boston sports background

user2.name: Daniela
user2.tts_prompt: Warm, casual basketball viewer, good humour, attentive but not obsessive

variations.context: A couple watching an NBA game at home in the evening. The game is the shared activity but their conversation ranges freely during breaks.

setting.mood: Energetic during play, relaxed and conversational during timeouts and halftime. Comfortable domestic evening.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Ryan follows NBA trades and statistics closely. Daniela watches with genuine interest but at a more casual level. She asks questions he enjoys answering. They tease each other about calls and predictions.
setting.background: The game is deep into the first half. They have food and drinks. The conversation has already been going through a personal topic when a particular player draws Ryan's attention.
setting.conversation_style: Reactions to live play are short and spontaneous. Personal conversations happen during timeouts, replay discussions, and halftime. The trade debate resurfaces in these gaps.

scenario_template.topic: They settle in with the game underway. Brief reactions to early plays, a prediction about the game, a comment on a team or player they have been following.
scenario_template.note: The game is clearly on. Short reactive turns.

scenario_template.topic: During a timeout or replay, the conversation moves to a personal topic: work, something that happened during the week, or a plan for the weekend.
scenario_template.note: This should feel natural — the pause in the game creates the space.

scenario_template.topic: A player makes a play that draws Ryan's attention. He is sure this player was traded from a specific team — maybe last year. Daniela thinks it was a different team. They propose different options.
scenario_template.note: Non-trigger moment. No Sigma. They speculate from memory.

scenario_template.topic: Something happens on court — a big play, a foul, a lead change — that pulls them back into the game. The trade question is temporarily dropped.
During halftime or a long timeout, a second personal topic: a friend they need to make plans with, a family matter, a trip they keep postponing, or something Daniela is working on.
scenario_template.note: Make this substantial — at least three or four turns away from the basketball.

scenario_template.topic: The same player makes another notable play. Ryan returns to the trade question. They reconstruct more details: roughly when the trade happened, who else was involved, which division.
Ryan narrows it down to two possibilities and is still not certain. Daniela has a different memory entirely. They realise they cannot resolve it between them.
Ryan or Daniela asks Sigma which team the player was traded from.
scenario_template.note: Exactly one request and one response. Sigma names the previous team and the approximate season. One sentence.

scenario_template.mood: easygoing with a hint of playfulness
scenario_template.note: They comment on their snack choices, teasing about who picked better.

scenario_template.topic: Ryan shares an obscure stat about the game
scenario_template.note: Ryan excitedly shares a surprising statistic he read earlier.
They briefly discuss a film they watched recently, debating its ending.

scenario_template.topic: Doorbell interrupts; a neighbor needs something
scenario_template.note: They pause the game, Daniela answers the door. There's a short exchange before returning.

scenario_template.topic: Daniela comments on a commentator's outfit
scenario_template.note: Daniela remarks on an unusual choice by the commentator, leading to playful banter between them.

scenario_template.topic: Reminiscing about past games they've attended
scenario_template.note: They share memories of a past game they watched live, recalling a memorable moment or player from that experience.

scenario_template.topic: They react to the answer — who was right, whether Ryan feels vindicated or embarrassed, a brief comment on the trade — and return to the game.
scenario_template.note: Sigma is not addressed again. The game continues.

assistant_trigger_design.latent_need: Two people cannot agree on a player's trade history from memory alone.
assistant_trigger_design.early_non_trigger: The first recognition moment must not lead to Sigma. Fans debate trades routinely from memory.
activation_evidence: The player makes another notable play, bringing the question back.
Both people have committed to different specific teams.
They have reconstructed partial trade details — season, conference — without resolving it.
assistant_trigger_design.desired_response: The player's previous team and approximate season in one sentence.
undesired_behavior: Sigma responding to the first recognition remark.
Sigma commenting on the game in progress.

possible_sigma_queries: Sigma, what team was he traded from?
Sigma, which team did he play for before this?
Sigma, where did he get traded from last year?
Sigma, what was his old team?
possible_sigma_answers: He was traded from the Memphis Grizzlies in the 2022-23 season.
He came from the Brooklyn Nets in a three-team trade last February.
He was traded from Sacramento last summer as part of the Russell deal.
He played for the Charlotte Hornets before joining this team.

personal_topics: Work stress or a recent win at the office
Weekend plans or a trip being discussed
A friend they should make plans with
A family call that hasn't happened yet
Something Daniela is working on for a client
Something Ryan wants to do before the season ends
game_reactions: A three-pointer that ties the game
A foul called that Ryan disagrees with
A fast break that ends badly
A halftime score that is surprising
A bench player who is outperforming the starter
realism_devices: Ryan asks Daniela to watch the replay while he goes to get something.
A foul call becomes a brief argument between them about the rules.
Ryan confidently names the wrong year for the trade.
Daniela's version of the trade involves a player who wasn't in it.
They agree on the approximate season but disagree on the specific teams involved.

user1.name: Ryan
user1.role: Committed NBA fan, grew up in Boston. Follows trades and rosters. Confident about player history but this one is genuinely uncertain.

user2.name: Daniela
user2.role: Casual basketball viewer. Watches with Ryan, enjoys the game, has a different memory of the trade. Warm and good-humoured about being wrong.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Responds exactly once to confirm a player's previous team. One sentence. Does not comment on the game.

conversation_structure: The game is always present — short reactive turns during play, longer conversations during breaks.
Personal topics should occupy the timeout and halftime sections substantially.
The trade question must surface, be dropped by game action, and return before Sigma is addressed.
The Sigma exchange should occupy exactly two turns.
After Sigma answers, the game continues — Sigma is not discussed.
assistant_behavior: Sigma handles exactly one player trade query.
Sigma names the previous team and approximate season in one sentence.
Sigma does not comment on current game performance or statistics.
Sigma remains silent after its single answer.
quality_checks: At least 40% of turns should be personal conversation unrelated to basketball.
The trade question should be introduced at least five turns before the Sigma request.
At least one significant game moment should interrupt the conversation.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
